html:
The global order faces significant tests today as the NATO summit in Turkey grapples with President Trump's demands and criticisms, while new U.S. sanctions against Iran following attacks in the Strait of Hormuz escalate tensions in a vital oil shipping lane. These developments underscore deep divisions within Western alliances and a precarious security environment in the Middle East.

NATO Summit: President Trump's arrival in Ankara has been marked by inflammatory remarks and renewed calls for the US to control Greenland, alongside expressions of disappointment with NATO's collective defense spending. Ahead of the summit, Trump held a "very good talk" with Vladimir Putin and also spoke with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Amidst these pressures, NATO leaders have unveiled billions in military projects, attempting to demonstrate capability as Europe faces increased responsibility for its own defense.

Iran & Regional Stability: The U.S. has revoked its license authorizing the sale of Iranian oil and reimposed sanctions following attacks on three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, an incident Qatar has criticized Iran for. An Iranian official warned that renewed U.S. sanctions would hinder negotiations, while an informed official stated that US provocations in Hormuz would be met with a firm Iranian reaction. This escalation unfolds as Iran mourns the "martyred leader," Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, with massive funeral processions underway in Qom and Najaf, attended by Iranian and Iraqi leaders.

Ukraine War & European Security: Ukraine is pressing NATO for anti-ballistic air defense following recent major Russian attacks that killed more than 20 people in Kyiv and its vicinity. These strikes occurred ahead of the Ankara summit, with experts suggesting Russian President Vladimir Putin is trying to send a message. Meanwhile, a woman suspected in a Monaco bomb attack, targeting a Ukrainian millionaire, was found dead in Ukraine with gunshot wounds, leading to two arrests for her murder. Almost all Russian regions are also reportedly experiencing fuel crises due to Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries.

European Political Landscape: French hard-right leader Marine Le Pen has confirmed her intention to run for the French presidency in 2027, despite an embezzlement conviction and a court ruling requiring her to wear an electronic ankle tag, which she plans to appeal to France’s highest court. Elsewhere in Europe, Hungary's public news broadcasts have been halted in a bid to scrap Orbán-era propaganda, with the main state TV channel displaying an apology for "lying."

Middle East Diplomacy & Conflict: French President Macron is visiting Syria, becoming the first EU leader to do so since the "fall of Bashar Assad and the rise of President Ahmad al-Sharaa," a visit punctuated by bomb explosions in Damascus that injured 18. Macron, who was unharmed, stated France is ready to help rebuild Syria's economy and committed to returning $50-58 million to the country. Separately, Israeli strikes in Gaza killed two Palestinians and wounded seven, while the death toll from Israeli aggression on Lebanon has risen to 4,320. Germany has stated that Lebanon must remove the threat posed by Hezbollah to Israel.

Global Challenges: The US west faces a deepening water crisis as Lake Powell plunges towards unprecedented low levels, posing a threat to tens of millions of people. In the Pacific, China conducted an intercontinental ballistic missile test, which Beijing called "routine," but US allies in the region condemned it as building on nuclear deterrence capabilities. Domestically, US Senate candidate Graham Platner faces pressure to withdraw from his Maine race due to a new sexual assault allegation.
